To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
YouTube’s video player uses DASH as ABR streaming technology.

1) YouTube is using a DASH implementation that is receiver-driven, 2) YouTube’s video player is using an algorithm that adapts the consumed bitrate to the available download bandwidth, and 3) this algorithm is able to cope with the dynamic nature of Internet access.
YouTube’s traffic is highly dynamic, and that it is possible to characterize it in a reliable way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
YouTube’s traffic adaptation in order to provide the end-user with an optimal Quality of Experience.
the analysis of YouTube’s traffic behavior in order to improve the understanding and the management of the YouTube’s service.
the study of YouTube’s DASH traffic and its rate adaptation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, YouTube’s traffic adaptation is based on the available bandwidth and the video quality is not constant during the video playback, but it is adapted to the available bandwidth.
the YouTube’s traffic pattern is highly variable and dynamic, and the video quality is highly correlated to the allowed download bandwidth.
YouTube traffic is not only affected by the end-user’s download bandwidth, but also by the video’s content and its popularity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper provides a deep analysis of the YouTube’s DASH adaptation to dynamic environments and, in particular, the impact of the network’s download bandwidth in the video streaming quality.
this article provides a deep analysis of the traffic pattern and performance of YouTube’s DASH technology.
the proposed methodology and test-bed are able to characterize and evaluate YouTube’s traffic, and also provide information to ISPs about the allowed download bandwidth and YouTube’s video quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the download bandwidth is the most important parameter in YouTube traffic characterization and performance analysis, because it has an impact on the video quality perceived by the end-user.
YouTube’s traffic adaptation is highly dependent on the available bandwidth, and it can be used to estimate the end-user’s QoS.
YouTube’s DASH is not a simple ABR implementation, but a complex and dynamic one.
